t1kqejni.name: Protests over India election chief
t1kqejni.latestHeadline: India’s voter roll overhaul fuels citizenship fears: ‘what if they ask us to leave?’
t1kqejni.summary: On 2 October, thousands of people joined a Mumbai protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party that asked the election chief to resign. In the days after, police detained dozens of protesters over changes to voter rolls, and on 6 October opposition MPs were detained, with opposition leaders alleging that CEC Gyanesh Kumar manipulated the rolls to favour PM Narendra Modi's party. By 10 October, police had ordered a virtual shutdown of New Delhi ahead of a planned protest and the country's highest court intervened, and on 12 October opposition parties and supporters of the youth movement marched towards the Supreme Court over the removal of millions of names from voter lists. By 16 October, protests had intensified in New Delhi, with critics calling the voter list review politically motivated while the Election Commission and Modi's administration denied the allegations.

Mapping US chip supply chain: China accounts for far more than it appears, report says

t139atn9.summary: In early October, The Guardian reported that US authorities had arrested a California man, Greg Lui, for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China. He allegedly used false paperwork to move export-controlled gear from the US to third countries and then on to China. In mid-October, the South China Morning Post reported on a Semiconductor Industry Association report on the US chip supply chain. It found that China accounts for about 5 per cent of the equipment and materials directly supplied to the US chip industry by country of manufacture, but holds over 90 per cent of certain rare earths needed for chipmaking.

t1j5n1me.name: Yemen war and Houthi strikes
t1j5n1me.latestHeadline: Blast heard in Yemen’s Aden as Houthis claim attack on military camp
t1j5n1me.summary: On 4 October, Yemen's president announced an all-out war to reclaim land from the Houthis, amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition. Two days later, Saudi Arabia said three people were wounded when Houthi strikes hit the Jazan and Najran airports, and by 10 October Al Jazeera was reporting that fighting between government forces and the Houthis was intensifying. In mid-October, Saudi Arabia struck oil depots near Sana'a, Houthi missiles hit the Maashiq Palace in Aden, and the UAE reportedly agreed to re-enter the conflict, while Egypt, Pakistan and the UK moved to help defend Saudi Arabia. Between 19 and 21 October, a Houthi attack killed 53 people at a government training camp in Shabwa, Saudi Arabia postponed its Future Investment Initiative event after the attacks, and the Houthis claimed a missile attack on a military camp in Aden.

t1rn1bq5.summary: In early October, the euro fell to a 17-month low against the US dollar, with reports citing concerns about France's ability to bring its public finances in order and an announced snap election in Spain. France 24 reported that the currency had dropped nearly 7 percent from its peak in late January. In the week of October 22, French protests and mounting bond market pressure pushed France's 10-year government bond yield to a 24-year high. Around October 23, reports said French borrowing costs had surged as debt and political risks mounted, raising questions over whether the stress could spread across the euro zone, while Moody's left France's credit rating at Aa3.

t14axxk2.summary: In early October, Ukraine's leader condemned a Russian strike on a Turkish-owned boat carrying corn in the Black Sea, in which the captain was killed and 11 crew were rescued. Around October 6, Bulgaria searched for missing crew after drones hit two ships and the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank, and on October 7 Russian authorities said an attack by "unmanned boats" on a Liberian-flagged tanker off Sochi sparked a huge oil fire. By mid-October, Bulgaria's prime minister said another drone attack off its coast had hit two ships, including the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which was damaged. On October 20 Nato increased its Black Sea deployment, and on October 23 Romania blamed Russia after a drone sank the Comoros-flagged Khoryv, leaving one sailor dead and three missing.

t1ibmsov.latestHeadline: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia, setting oil facilities ablaze
t1ibmsov.summary: In early October, Ukraine's top sanctions official said Russia had imported fuel from South Korean ports, easing a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. On October 11, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv was ready to halt refinery strikes if Moscow stopped attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure, and US President Donald Trump said both sides had agreed to an "energy ceasefire." By October 16, Zelensky said Ukraine would resume the strikes he had paused to comply with a US demand, Russian authorities said a major refinery southeast of Moscow had been hit, and Trump called the strikes a "disgrace" that keeps global energy prices elevated. On October 18 and 19, reports described Ukraine launching more than 1,000 drones at Russian oil and other facilities, while Zelensky said Moscow continued to break the energy ceasefire.

t12s750z.summary: On October 7, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said big economies would have to make hard choices as soaring bond yields hit budgets. On October 11, Al Jazeera reported that the US-Israel war on Iran and its inflationary impact, along with high debt, would dominate the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok. By October 12, US Treasury yields had touched 24-year highs as a global bond sell-off picked up, with the 10-year at 5.36% and the 30-year at 5.73%, the highest for each since 2002. On October 13, yields fell as energy prices pulled back, while some analysts said investors were demanding a higher "term premium" to buy government debt, reflecting worries about debt levels and deficits.

t1qk19hr.summary: In early October, India's central bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, with BBC News and CNBC reporting that the move reflected growing inflation concerns. BBC News described it as part of a global shift towards tighter monetary policy as central banks battle inflation fuelled by Middle East conflict. CNBC also reported that HSBC and Goldman Sachs expect the RBI to raise rates again in December. In mid-October, CNBC reported that India's retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September, above estimates, marking the 11th straight month of increase.

tq9ru94.summary: In early October, India, Turkiye, Egypt and the US put forward ceasefire proposals, and US envoys were set to meet Ukrainian and European officials in Miami to discuss a new proposal to end the war. By around October 10, the Kremlin said drone attacks on Moscow during last month's election had undermined trilateral talks, while President Trump called for Ukraine to replace President Zelensky. In mid-October, tensions between Washington and Kyiv deepened as Russia and Ukraine traded strikes, with Zelensky saying the two sides were still in near-constant contact. tpnacn3.latestHeadline: Housing is flashing warning signs just as the Fed weighs more interest rate hikes
tpnacn3.summary: In early October, a softer jobs report and strong signaling from Fed officials lowered the odds of an interest rate change at the Federal Reserve's late-October meeting. Minutes released on October 7 showed policymakers had grown increasingly concerned about inflation risks at their September meeting, and a report the next day said a further rate rise was unlikely until the end of the year. In mid-October, the Cleveland Fed president said tighter monetary policy would be needed to bring down inflation, while Chairman Kevin Warsh suggested he wouldn't push to raise rates this month, though persistent inflation might force the Fed's hand. By October 20, housing data had deteriorated further in September as the Fed weighed more rate hikes.
